data.name: Mustafeed
data.gender_notes: Mustafeed is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘stf’, meaning to satiate or fulfill. In Islamic history, Mustafeed refers to those who have been granted sustenance and contentment by Allah. The name Mustafeed carries the meaning “Satiated, Fulfilled” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mustafeed usually hope their child will grow to embody satiated, fulfilled and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes being filled with divine blessings and provision from Allah.
data.etymology: Mustafeed belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Satiated, Fulfilled.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mustafeed total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 10, Page 141 The name Mustafeed carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: This is the name of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, the companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He was the chief of the Banu Aws tribe in Madinah, and was the leader of their army during the Battle of Hunayn. After the battle, the Prophet (pbuh) granted him the title 'Mustafeed' (the quenched).

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham, Sirah Ibn Hisham, Volume 1, Page 377 The name Mustafeed carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: This is the name of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, the second caliph of Islam. He was given this title during the Battle of Uhud when he was seriously injured and the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) prayed for his recovery, saying 'O Allah, make him Mustafeed (the refreshed) from his injury.' The name stuck with him afterwards.
